subject: baku
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: baku, the dream-eating tapir spirit.
Style: ukiyo-e woodblock print.
reasoning:
I'm designing a baku creature—tapir body, elephant trunk, tiger paws, ox tail, lion mane—rendered in ukiyo-e style with flat indigo, vermilion, cream, and black outlines plus wave and cloud motifs, starting with the skeleton rig and planning a moderately sized module using the core SDK.

Mapping out the full skeleton: spine chain from hips to chest, neck and head joints, a curling trunk chain, jaw joint, and leg chains with hip, knee, ankle, and foot points sized to reach the ground with natural bend directions for front and hind limbs.

For the body, I'll sweep the skin along the spine path with varying radii for a chunky profile, then color it like a tapir with indigo bands at the front and rear and a cream saddle in the middle, adding small wave motifs in that ukiyo-e style on the saddle area.

Adding seigaiha wave discs and the flame-like mane blades...

Now I'm planning the neck as a separate chain branching off the spine's last joint, with its own catmull path and tapering radius, then a head joint attached at the neck's end with a forward-down orientation to keep the silhouette continuous.

For the head itself, I'm shaping a tapir-like skull using a scaled sphere plus a frustum-shaped upper snout positioned forward of the head joint, coloring the skull indigo with cream-rimmed ears and planning a separate lower jaw piece.

The jaw attaches as its own joint angled down and forward from the head, shaped as a cream frustum box. For the trunk, I'm sprouting a curved chain from the snout tip using a catmull path that dips down and forward in three spans, swept with a tapering radius and a vermilion tip band plus small cream ridge rings, parented to the head joint.

Now I'm setting up eyes using head-local offsets (forward, up, left) to place almond-shaped cream eye whites with indigo-black pupils and bold outlines, pushing the pupils slightly outward for a ukiyo-e look.

Then I'm building the ears as extruded oval outlines in the head's local plane, facing forward, with a layered look: a thicker cream rim behind and a slightly smaller indigo shape offset in front to give depth.

Now I'm thinking about adding small curved horns or tusks swept along bezier curves in ivory tones, plus a mane along the neck and back using flame-shaped blades in vermilion and gold, and a spiral-curled tuft at the shoulders for a lion-like touch.

Placing ukiyo-e inspired spiral curls in indigo-cream and gold around the chest, shoulders, and hips on both flanks, then designing the tail as an ox-like tuft curling upward from the hips.

I'm now adding a cluster of small vermilion and gold spikes to form the tuft at the tail tip, arranging them in a ring pattern around the final joint point.

Next I'm working out the legs, using tapering sweep radii down to the paws, then shaping each paw as a flattened sphere positioned at the foot point with claws and toe stripes for the tiger details.

Adding ankle bands as vertical torus rings oriented along the leg axis, placed at the ankle joints, plus cream stripe rings along the legs. I'm settling on indigo legs with cream paws and indigo claws to match the ukiyo-e palette.

I'm skipping ground or cloud elements entirely, keeping the composition minimal, but considering a sumi stripe along the spine ridge and maybe a tiny vermilion seal mark as a decorative signature touch.

Adding tiny glowing wisps near the trunk tip using the glow kit. Now moving to the mouth and jaw: a lower jaw shape beneath the upper snout, with the trunk extending forward from the snout tip, and I'm positioning the skull sphere and frustum snout boxes relative to the head joint and forward direction.

Working out trunk curl points and head positioning in model space, then setting radii tapering from 0.075 to 0.03. Now I'm figuring out body proportions—spine height, leg length showing below the belly, and hip socket placement relative to the body radius.

Defining the leg chains next, computing hip-to-foot distances for hind and front legs with bend directions, then naming each joint (hip, knee, ankle, foot) for the chain builder.

Setting up sweep radii arrays for leg thickness, side letter logic to distinguish left/right limbs, and starting to plan body coloring bands along the spine.

I'll skip the sector stripes and instead scatter seigaiha patterns on the cream region, filtering hits by surface normal and z-position along the spine to target the belly/back area. For each matched hit, I'll stack discs as cylinders with decreasing radius to form a layered scale motif.

Then for the mane, I'll sweep chains along the neck and back, extruding a flame-shaped outline with sharp points to give it a stylized spiky texture.

I need to position the flame at the blade root using an offset along the surface normal, but realize the offset function returns a plain vector that loses the bone reference, so I'll need to pass the bone explicitly to keep the rigging intact.

Then I'm working out the dorsal crest sweep along the spine—smaller alternating vermilion and gold flames placed with a restricted range (roughly 0.05 to 0.85) along the body path, using a two-layer approach where a larger vermilion blade sits beneath a smaller offset gold blade for visual depth.

For the tail, I'm chaining a sweep with tapering radii down to 0.03, capped with a spiked ring tuft. For the eyes, I'm computing positions on the skull sphere using forward/up/left offsets, checking the math against the ellipsoid surface equation to make sure the eye sockets sit just outside the skull, then layering a dark outline ring over a small eyeball sphere.

Now I'm layering concentric eye spheres outward from the socket base — outline, then white, then a vermilion iris, then a dark pupil, each nudged slightly forward and outward in sequence. I'm also sketching a vermilion brow sweep curving over each eye using three head-local points, and starting to lay out an oval-shaped ear outline anchored near the top-back of the skull.

Positioning the ears...

Working out the forehead mark's orientation and thickness axis so the diamond shape sits flush on top of the head...

Now I'm adding whiskers for the baku-style face -- a pair of long, curling gold strands sweeping back from the snout corners, thin and flowing in an ukiyo-e inspired arc.

Next I'm placing small downward tusks near the jaw, cream-colored bone cones angled outward along the trunk, then starting on curved horns rising and bending back from the crown using bezier control points.

Finishing the horn curves, repositioning the ears slightly outward to clear them, and giving the horns a tapered gold color. Then I'm working out how to add ridge rings along the trunk's sweep path using small torus shapes oriented to the trunk's tangent direction.

Keeping the face cream-toned around the muzzle. For the chest and hip spiral motifs, I'm placing them by sampling a surface hit point on the flank, pushing the spiral center slightly outward along the normal, and orienting the spiral axis along that normal with a small radius.

Finishing the spiral sweep with 1.6 turns, gold color, and guarding against null hits by checking if the hit exists before proceeding. I'm confirming the azimuth convention so positive s maps to +X, then deciding to skip the seal motif and move toward layering seigaiha waves, curls, and maybe a vermilion cloud instead.

For the seal cartouche, I'm placing nested boxes at the hit location on the flank -- a vermilion outer box, a smaller cream inset, and a tiny sumi accent -- to form a stamped ukiyo-e style mark. Then I'm adding a few small glowing dream orb spheres near the head/trunk area at scattered local positions to give a dreamlike accent.

Deciding to skip the spiral wisp trail and ring halo for simplicity, keeping just the glow orbs. For the feet, I'm adding small spike claws (cream colored) in front of each toe, angled slightly downward and forward with a thin cone shape, positioned relative to the foot/toe bone tip.

Adding leg bands with tapered torus rings, using vermilion and gold tones at the ankle and knee, oriented along each leg segment's direction.

Confirming chain naming works correctly for spine, neck, trunk, and tail segments, then setting up the hips as root with a spine role, attaching the head to the neck's end joint with its own role, and defining the jaw role before working out the neck path coordinates.

I'm sketching the neck curve so it connects into the chest at the right point, parenting it off the spine chain, and tuning the radii so the head sits proportionally against the neck. Then I'm laying out the spine's catmull curve points and body radii, checking the span count matches the knot points and that the lowest body radius keeps the silhouette grounded.

The mane needs its orientation vectors set so the blade profile reads correctly in side view, curving backward like a flame outline. I'm defining a flame-generator helper that takes a position and bone reference, loosely typing the params since the exact bone type isn't pinned down yet, and offsetting the flame slightly along the up axis before pulling in the glow import.

Simplifying the outline typing...

Now I'm starting to write the actual builder code: setting up color constants, sphere helpers, and the body structure with hips, spine chain, and a swept body mesh with indigo coloring.

For the legs, I'm looping over left/right sides, computing hip and limb points for the hind legs, and building chains with parent/role metadata and unique joint names per side, checking that polyline point arrays are accepted directly by the chain function.

Writing sweep and paw code...

Setting up the seigaiha ring colors and radii with alternating indigo, pale, and vermillion hues at decreasing sizes, with slightly increasing heights for layering. Then moving to the metadata export step.
